Preserve native STOP/recovery and source custody through the installed Fleet package. Graceful cancellation lets Alpha finish its original interruption receipt and cleanup, with bounded kill escalation and strict native inspection retained. Protected imports and the native bridge execute private, retained Git-verified Alpha bytes; runtime custody and final fingerprints bind that same capture.

Add the authenticated final public-package consumer and a separate later live-site verifier. Fleet installs normally from immutable public assets; companion packages supply complete source without checkout gap filling. Keep the Alpha wheel CLI distinct from native source-package execution. Preserve the original service, GUI, grants, STOP/recovery, history, two disposable payment routes and independent collectors.

Current head: `4423fa0602229c6d9ce6e198dd68fca0bac37ba3`, tree `ed382a6ac343bc6b1759af072bca4cb1aa031c92`.

- Recovery waits for rendered controls and the existing enabled-button assertion before reading the plan; acceptance assertions and time limits are unchanged.

The finite24-path TI inventory refresh changes only its source-pins row. Historical captures stay historical; fresh exact-source native capture is required.
- Jobs live metadata verifies `catalog.json/revision`, with explicit unavailable served version and separate release-version context. Fleet verifies website T in build-info and separately hashes/binds release.json to actual released software S and its version. Alpha and Manager retain served-version equality. All release/connected/Pages/source/download/EN-FR/console/screenshot checks remain.
- Setup failure now deregisters any installed hooks and removes only the newly created, reproducible source captures, including failures before hook registration. An existing caller directory remains untouched. Three added ordinary regressions cover capture-write failures, captured-module load failure and existing-directory preservation; original tests remain exact. Both affected TI inventory rows refresh.
- The continuation changes exactly12 existing regular leaves relative to66940b6; all6,901 others retain their Git objects and modes. The five live-metadata blobs are exactly the independently reviewed b550 proposal.

Validation and remaining gates: original669 completed all10 workflow groups, including both native architectures, both saved-package journeys, browser/archive audits, Linux1.1.5 and repository/integration checks. Those observations remain historical. The prepared b550 metadata proposal passed seven benign units and syntax checks; that does not qualify this integrated head442. Fresh442 configured review and every original exact-head source/native/browser/saved-package/archive gate are required. [Prepared metadata proof](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGI-Fleet-Linux/pull/61#issuecomment-6293457346), [retained continuation evidence](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGI-Fleet-Linux/tree/8bc7c4430dafd7112399df7ed6fb72e26b37e5db/docs/release-evidence/ti-compatible-set-20261019/continuation-ci).

Manager v1.19.5 is public. Alpha/Jobs main publication remains pending; these candidate pins make no release claim. Required eligible independent owner review under [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGI-Fleet-Linux/blob/4423fa0602229c6d9ce6e198dd68fca0bac37ba3/CONTRIBUTING.md) remains absent. Automatic approval review rejected that owner-review lane for possible cybersecurity risk; it has not been retried, rerouted or replaced with configured/static advisory review. Normal merge and all three Fleet software publications remain gated.

The ONE final public installed-package journey, actual installed-file D, complete E, separate reviewed website T and final four-site HTTP/UI observations remain outstanding. No Mainnet signing/transactions, funded work, activation, irreversible deletion or paid storage commitment is included.
